Here is a sample solution in Python:

```python
def f(N: int, members: List[Tuple[str, int]], M: int, changes: List[str]) -> int:
    # This solution is based on dynamic programming approach.
    scores = [m[1] for m in members]  # Copy the scores from members list to scores list.
    for change in changes:
        if "+" in change:  # If operation is "+ t b".
            t, b = change.split()  # Split the operation into two parts.
            scores.append(int(t[1:]) + min(scores))  # Add the new score into scores list.
        elif "-" in change:  # If operation is "- t".
            t = change.split()[1]  # Split the operation into two parts.
            scores.remove(int(t[1:]))  # Remove the score from scores list.
    return max(scores)  # Return the maximum score.
```

The time complexity for this solution is O(N), in which N is the total number of operations to be performed. This is because we only make one pass over the operation list to update the scores list. So, the time complexity is linear.

The space complexity is also O(N), where N is the maximum size of the scores list. This is because we store all the scores in the scores list. Since the maximum size of the scores list can be up to 50,000 (based on the problem constraints), the space complexity is quadratic.
